answer: A registry issues agent credentials only after a hardware-rooted attestation plus a posted bond; randomized challenges are committed through a Merkle prism and an anonymized audit plume records pass/fail, so misconduct creates a portable reputation ripple. Faking N identities costs N bonds, N attestations, and N audit exposures, while per-credential rewards and non-transferable reputation are capped; splitting one resource pool across identities therefore raises costs without raising total expected reward. Limitation: compromised enclaves or colluding attestors can still mint identities.
